page.layout: Running head at top left: "D. PETRI MARTYRIS", page number at top right. Main text in one block: a Latin verse poem of six couplet stanzas, then a centred author heading "IOANNIS CONRADI Fabricij." and a second poem of five couplet stanzas. No marginal notes, no footnotes. Bottom right: catchword "N". Bottom left: a faint signature.

l.i: Christiq[?], infestos vt murus aheneus hostes, Voce sacri late fudit Euangelij. Testis erit Latium, & florens Germania testis, Anglia testis erit, Gallia testis erit.
Sed iuuat immodicos nil quidquam fundere fletus, Fata velut cunctis non subeunda forent. Maiores laudem factis peperere perennem, Hic peperit scriptis nomina digna suis.
Illi Christigenam testati sanguine mentem, Ipse tibi Martyr dogmate martyr erit. Vna dies nequijt Heroas tollere cunctos, Non omnes doctos abstulit vna dies.

Martyra mors Petrum nostris subduxit ocellis Clausit & exiguo membra sepulta loco. Quo se grex ouium tanto pastore perempto Vertet, & unde sibi pabula nota petet? Quis doctos vltra simili sermone docebit? An cuiquam est[?] tantis mens cumulata bonis? Non dubitanda loquor, percellimur omine tanto, Et vereor mœstas urbis adesse dies. Summe Deus pastorq; gregis submitte labori Pastores, templi commiserere tui.

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The printed "est" in line 6 of the second poem has an unusual form, read as "est" with doubt. Show-through of the reverse page (faint text in the right and lower areas) and the bottom-left signature are uncertain and were not transcribed as text. The "+" after "tui." appears to be a printer's mark and was not copied. The catchword "N" is a single letter and may be a reference mark rather than a catchword.
